SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
REPORT
（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE. C. Dept. REGISTRATION. No. I. O. D. 7248. April 26th 1930. 29-4-30.）
Subject (in full) M. A. Jacobs versus E. Schmidt.
Made by D. S. I. Robinson Forwarded by （签名）
Sir,
I beg to report that on my advice Mr. Jacobs wrote to
Schmidt and arranged a rendezvous to ascertain definitely what
Schmidt wanted of him (letter & reply attached).
I interviewed Mr. Bryan who stated that even if a charge
was preferred against Schmidt it would probably result in a cau-
tion and accordingly on his advice both D. S. Pryde and myself
were in opposite seats to Jacobs and Schmidt at their meeting
at the Astor House at 6:30 p.m. 25-4-30.
Very little however could be overheard and an appointment
was made for 10:30 a.m. this inst. at Jacobs' office.
Schmidt attended and I approached him, ascertained that he
was German and he readily admitted writing the letter.
I informed him that if he had any monetary dispute with
Jacobs he had his legal remedy in suing him at the British
Court and advised him against sending any further similar letters.
This he agreed to do.
Subsequently Mr. Davis of the N. China Daily News informed
me that he really knew very little about Jacobs except that he
was evidently a rolling stone who probably had seen more affluent
days. He is not entrusted with any money of the firm and seems
to be of the type that cannot get out of the habit of living
at the rate of double the amount of his monthly salary. It is
possible that there is something owing to Schmidt although Jacobs
strongly denies it.
I am, Sir,
Yours obediently,
（签名）
D. S. I.
（批：Per / My）

上海公共租界工部局警务处。
报告
（印：上海公共租界工部局警务处。C. 部门 登记处。编号 I. O. D. 7248。1930年4月26日。1930年4月29日。）
事由（全称）M. A. Jacobs 诉 E. Schmidt。
由 D. S. I. Robinson 呈报 转呈人 （签名）
先生，
谨此报告，经我建议，Jacobs 先生致信 Schmidt 并安排了一次会面，以确切查明 Schmidt 对他有何要求（信件及回复附后）。
我约谈了 Bryan 先生，他表示即使对 Schmidt 提出指控，结果可能也只是予以警告；因此，根据他的建议，在 1930年4月25日下午6:30 于礼查饭店（Astor House）举行的 Jacobs 与 Schmidt 的会面中，D. S. Pryde 和我本人分别坐在 Jacobs 和 Schmidt 对面的座位上。
然而，几乎听不到什么内容，双方约定于本月上午10:30 在 Jacobs 的办公室再次会面。
Schmidt 出席了会面，我上前与他接触，确认他是德国人，他爽快地承认了那封信是他写的。
我告知他，如果他与 Jacobs 有任何金钱纠纷，他可以通过向英国法院提起诉讼来获得法律救济，并劝告他不要再发送任何类似的信件。
他同意照办。
随后，《字林西报》（North China Daily News）的 Davis 先生告诉我，他对 Jacobs 的了解确实很少，只知道他显然是一个居无定所的人，可能曾经有过较为富裕的日子。公司并未将任何资金交托给他管理，他似乎属于那种无法摆脱按月薪两倍标准生活习性的人。虽然 Jacobs 强烈否认，但有可能确实欠 Schmidt 一些款项。
此致，
敬礼，
（签名）
D. S. I.
（批注：Per / My）
（批注：D.S. (5/8) / 知悉）

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
File No.
Central Station,
REPORT
Date April 22nd, 1930
Subject (in full) M. A. Jacobs versus E. Schmidt.
Made by C. D. I. Quayle Forwarded by [Signature]
Sir,
With reference to the attached I beg to report that D.S.I.
Robinson interviewed Mr. M. A. Jacobs in order to ascertain what
he knows of the writer of the letter. Jacobs states that he em-
ployed Schmidt as a commission agent in Bangkok and that there
was considerable trouble between them over financial matters the
whole affair culminating in Jacobs putting an advertisement in
the Bangkok papers to the effect that he had dispensed with the
services of Schmidt whilst the latter also inserted an advertise-
ment to the effect that Jacobs owed him money.
Jacobs admits that he was in financial straits when he left
Bangkok and owed certain amounts of money to various persons,
which he states he intends to repay when he is in a position to
do so.
He wants to proceed as far as possible against Schmidt but
it was explained to him that the letter written to him hardly
justifies a charge of blackmail in view of the financial relations
formerly existing between them.
He was advised to see Schmidt and ascertain exactly what are
the latter's demands.
P.O. Box 843 to which correspondence for Schmidt is to be
addressed is registered in the name of Stephen A. Pappadopulo, No. 142 Boone
Road.
5/6/30. B.
Better see M.A. in re. The Letter
contains threats. What nationality
D. D. O. "A" is Schmidt?
[Signature]
C. D. I.

档案号
中央巡捕房，
报告
日期 1930年4月22日
事由（全称）M. A. Jacobs 诉 E. Schmidt。
由 C. D. I. Quayle 呈报 转呈人 [签名]
先生，
关于附件内容，谨此报告，D.S.I. Robinson 约谈了 M. A. Jacobs 先生，以查明他对信件作者的了解情况。Jacobs 称，他曾雇佣 Schmidt 在曼谷（Bangkok）担任佣金代理人，两人之间因财务问题发生了不少纠纷，整个事件最终以 Jacobs 在曼谷报纸上刊登广告告终，大意是他已不再需要 Schmidt 的服务，而后者也刊登了一则广告，大意是 Jacobs 欠他钱。
Jacobs 承认，他在离开曼谷时陷入财务困境，并欠下若干人的款项，他表示一旦有能力偿还， intends 打算归还这些债务。
他希望尽可能对 Schmidt 采取法律行动，但已向他解释，鉴于他们以前存在的财务关系，写给他的这封信几乎不足以构成勒索指控。
建议他会见 Schmidt，确切了解后者的要求。
Schmidt 的通信收件地址为邮政信箱 843 号，该信箱是以 Stephen A. Pappadopulo 的名义注册的，地址为布恩路（Boone Road）142号。
1930年5月6日。B.
最好就信件事宜会见 M.A.
信中带有威胁。Schmidt
是什么国籍？
D. D. O. "A"
[签名]
C. D. I.

E. SCHMIDT
Shanghai, 23rd April 1930.
P.O.Box 843.

Mr. M.A.Jacobs,
c/o North China Daily News,
S H A N G H A I.

Dear Sir,

Referring to your letter of the 22nd instant,
I prefer to meet you on the day and time mentioned in
your above letter say Friday 25th inst.,at 6-30 p.m.,
in the Astor House, corner ground floor.

I consider this place more convenient for both
of us.

Yours truly
E. Schmidt

在礼查饭店（Astor House），底层拐角处。

我认为这个地方对我们双方都更为方便。

I am in receipt of your letter. Whilst admitting

E. SCHMIDT
Shanghai, 17th April 1930.
P/O
P.O.Box 546.

Mr. F.A. Jacobs,
c/o North China Daily News,
S H A N G H A I.

Dear Sir,

I have arrived here from Bangkok via
Singapore and after some careful searches I have
found out that you are here, working in the NORTH
CHINA DAILY NEWS.

I do not want to remind you about the many
cases that you left unsettled in Singapore and Bank
kok, although your creditors as well as the police
will be too glad to know that I found you at last.

I suppose that you will prefer an amicable
settlement rather than force me to apply to the
police of the SETTLEMENT.

I wait for your urgent reply and hope that
you will not give me the trouble to use the Shanghai
Press in order to describe your exploits in the above
two places.

Yours truly
E. Schmidt

REGISTERED

E. SCHMIDT
上海，1930年4月17日。
P/O
邮政信箱 546 号。

F.A. Jacobs 先生，
转交《字林西报》，
上 海。

尊敬的先生：

我已从曼谷经由
新加坡抵达此地，经过一番仔细查找，我
发现您在这里，在《字林西报》工作。

我不想提醒您那些在新加坡和曼
谷未解决的诸多案件，尽管您的债权人以及警察
都会非常高兴得知我终于找到了您。

我想您会更倾向于友好和解，而不是
迫使我去求助于租界警方。

我等待您的紧急回复，并希望您
不要给我添麻烦，迫使我利用上海
报刊来描述您在这两个地方的所作所为。

您真诚的
E. Schmidt
